In January 1933, Poland was home to the largest Jewish population in Europe: 3,000,000 people.

By 1945, that community would be almost entirely destroyed.

This is the map of European Jewry in the year Hitler took power — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The numbers on this map are staggering in scale. Poland: 3,000,000. The USSR: roughly 2,525,000. Germany: about 565,000. Romania: 980,000. Hungary: 445,000. Together, Central and Eastern Europe held the vast majority of the world's Jewish population.

2/ Western Europe looked very different. France counted around 225,000 Jews, the UK 300,000, the Netherlands 160,000 — much smaller communities, many of them recent arrivals from the east fleeing earlier waves of pogroms and persecution.

3/ Germany's 565,000 Jews in 1933 were a tiny fraction of the country's 65 million people — well under 1%. Many were assimilated, decorated WWI veterans, prominent in science, medicine and the arts. None of that offered protection after January 30, 1933.

4/ The Baltic states show how deep this history ran: Lithuania's 155,000 Jews made up close to 7% of the population, with Vilnius so central to Jewish learning it was nicknamed the "Jerusalem of Lithuania."

5/ By the time the Second World War ended in 1945, the Holocaust had killed roughly six million Jews — about two-thirds of Europe's 1933 Jewish population. Poland's community of three million was reduced by over 90%.

6/ This map isn't just geography — it's a snapshot of entire civilizations, taken the year before the countdown to their destruction began.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
